name: Plaça de Sant Felip Neri (bombing of 30 January 1938)
story: On 30 January 1938 Italian aircraft from Mallorca bombed the old city of Barcelona. One bomb fell on this small square, where the church crypt was used as an air-raid shelter by the neighbouring school and children who had been evacuated from Madrid. As rescuers dug survivors out of the rubble, a second bomb struck. Forty-two people were killed, most of them children, making it one of the deadliest single incidents of the city's bombing. For decades the damage to the church front was said to come from executions; today a plaque records the true cause.
see: The church façade is still pitted with shrapnel scars, and a plaque remembers the victims; the rest of the square is unchanged.
plan: Free, always accessible, in the Gothic Quarter a few minutes from the cathedral; a quiet place, so please be respectful as the school still uses the square.
